newsitem.title: FRANCE: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV SETS TWO RECORDS, PROMISES MORE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV SETS TWO RECORDS, PROMISES MORE.

text.p: Denis Pankratov, denied two world records in Paris last year because of a dope test blunder, set two more in two days at this year's edition of the same short-course World Cup meeting over the weekend and warned that others could follow soon.
The Russian double Olympic champion clocked 51.78 seconds in the 100 metres butterfly on Sunday, bettering the record of 51.93 he set last Wednesday in Imperia, Italy.

On Saturday, the double Olympic champion had set another world record by clocking 23.35 in the 50 metres butterfly, improving the previous mark of 23.45 set by Briton Mark Foster in December 1995 in Sheffield, England.

It was sweet recompense for the Russian, who had broken both the 100 and 200 metres butterfly short-course world marks at last year's final World Cup meeting in Paris, only to be denied the records because French meet organisers had run out of bottles to administer the dope tests necessary for ratification.
"I like this swimming pool," he said after setting his fourth short-course world record in just nine days in the last three meetings of the eight-venue World Cup series in 25-metre pools.
"It's one of the fastest in Europe. It's certainly one of my favourites and I'm trying to make the most of it."
Pankratov began his record spree in Gelsenkirchen, Germany, on February 1 when he clocked 1:52.64 in the 200 metres butterfly.
"I don't feel bitter about what happened to me here last year because the Olympics then brought me some consolation," he said, referring to the dope test fiasco.
Pankratov said breaking records would be his main goal this year.
"I think I can do better in all three events (50, 100 and 200 metres butterfly)," he said. "In the 50 metres, I think I can go under 23 (seconds)."
When breaking both records in Paris, Pankratov swam under the water for most of the first 25 metres, surfacing only once shortly before the turn.
"I could go just as fast on top of the water but I would lose more energy," he explained.
The Russian was not the only one to shine in Paris.
Claudia Poll, Costa Rica's 200 metres freestyle Olympic champion, won four freestyle events and handed China's Le Jingyi a rare defeat in the 100 freestyle on Sunday.

Poll, who won the 200 and 800 freestyle on Saturday, took the 100 freestyle in 54.56, with Le a well-beaten second in 55.23 -- way outside the 53.01 world mark held by Le, the world and Olympic champion at the distance.
Dutchman Marcel Wouda bettered the short-course world record he had set in Gelsenkirchen the previous weekend, clocking 4:05.41 in the 400 metres individual medley on Saturday.
Wouda just missed a medal at last year's Atlanta Olympics but swept all three individual medley titles at the European short-course championships in Rostock, Germany, last December.
German Mark Warnecke, reigning 100 metres breaststroke world short-course champion, had earlier broken his own 50 metres breaststroke short-course world record with a time of 26.97 seconds.
